proof_summary: Matching Rule 167’s zero update with the XOR form of Pascal’s recursion shows that its zero cells at time \(t\) occur exactly at \(x=2-t+2j\) where \(\binom{t-1}{j}\) is odd; parity reduction of the resulting near-central binomial coefficient shows that the middle bit is zero exactly when \(t\) is a power of two. Since \(n\mid 2^{n+1}\) holds exactly when \(n\) is a power of two, the floor term detects precisely that zero bit, and appending the bit to a binary prefix gives the claimed recurrence.
